stem.en:
Text 1
A good teacher corrects a mistake the moment it is made. If a student practices a wrong method for a week, the wrong method becomes a habit, and undoing a habit takes far longer than learning the right way at the start.

Text 2
In my cooking class, I let new students make mistakes and find them on their own. When a sauce they make burns or splits, they look for the reason, and they remember the lesson far better than if I had stopped them at the first wrong step.

Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 1 most likely respond to the approach described in Text 2?

options.en: By warning that the students may turn their mistakes into habits before they find them
By agreeing that people remember lessons best when they find their mistakes themselves
By claiming that cooking students make far fewer mistakes than other students do
By arguing that teachers should never let their students practice on their own

why.en: Text 1 says a wrong method practiced for long "becomes a habit" that is hard to undo, so its author would fear that mistakes left uncorrected become habits.
why.uz: Text 1 uzoq mashq qilingan notoʻgʻri usul «becomes a habit» deydi, demak u tuzatilmagan xatolar odatga aylanishidan xavotir oladi.
why.ru: Text 1: неверный способ «becomes a habit», которую трудно исправить; автор побоялся бы, что неисправленные ошибки станут привычкой.

Fewer young people in our town are learning the old craft of carpet weaving. The reason is money: a carpet takes months to make, and buyers will not pay a fair price for that much work.

It is true that few young people now learn to weave carpets. Yet carpets from our town still sell for good prices at the market. The young leave the craft because it is taught only by long apprenticeship in one house, and few teenagers will sit at one loom for years before they make anything of their own.

Which choice best describes how Text 1 and Text 2 differ?

options.en: They agree that fewer young people learn the craft but give different reasons for it.
Text 1 says that carpets sell well, while Text 2 says that they do not sell at all.
Text 1 is about young weavers, while Text 2 is about the people who buy carpets.
Text 1 wants weaving taught in the schools of the town, while Text 2 wants it taught at home.

why.en: Both accept that few young people learn weaving; Text 1 blames low prices, while Text 2 says carpets sell well and blames the long apprenticeship.

stem.en:

Young chess players improve fastest by playing as many games as they can. Each game shows them positions they have never seen, and the more positions a player has met, the faster she sees a good move. Our club should hold quick tournaments every week.

Text 2
Playing many games certainly gives a young player experience. But a player who never stops to study her lost games keeps making the same mistakes. Our club should play fewer games and spend the time going over them move by move.

Based on the texts, both authors would most likely agree with which statement?

options.en: Playing games gives young players experience that helps them.
The club should hold quick tournaments for its players every week.
Studying lost games is a waste of time for a young player.
Young players learn nothing at all from the games they win.

why.en: Text 1 says each game shows new positions; Text 2 agrees that games "certainly" give experience. They differ on how much to play and study.

why.ru: Text 1: каждая партия показывает новые позиции; Text 2 согласен, что игры «certainly» дают опыт. Спорят, сколько играть и разбирать.

A neighborhood is safest when its streets are busy. Shops on the ground floor, people walking to work, children on the way to school: every passerby is a pair of eyes, and a street that is watched has little trouble.

Residents of our quiet lane have asked the council to close it to through traffic and put a gate at each end. A closed lane, they say, would keep strangers out and make their homes safer.

By agreeing that keeping strangers out is the best way to make a street safe
By suggesting that the residents should open shops on the ground floors of their homes
By claiming that quiet lanes have more trouble than any other kind of street

why.en: For Text 1, a busy street is safe because every passerby watches it; a gated lane with no passersby would have fewer eyes, so its author would object.

stem.en:

Some parents say that children should not get pocket money until they are twelve, because younger children will only waste it on sweets. I disagree. A child of eight who wastes her money on sweets and then cannot buy the book she wanted has learned something that no talk from a parent could teach.

Text 2
Pocket money teaches children how to handle money, and the earlier they start, the better. But a lesson needs a little help: a parent who sits down each week with an eight-year-old and talks about what she bought will see her waste far less.

Based on the texts, both authors would most likely agree with which statement?

options.en: Children can learn about handling money from having pocket money of their own.
Children under twelve will only waste their pocket money on sweets.
Talks with parents teach children more about money than spending it themselves does.
Children should get pocket money only after they have turned twelve.

why.en: Text 1 says a child who wastes her money "has learned something"; Text 2 says pocket money "teaches children how to handle money". The sweets view is one both reject.
why.uz: Text 1 pulini isrof qilgan bola «has learned something» deydi; Text 2 choʻntak puli «teaches children how to handle money» deydi. Shirinlik fikrini ikkalasi rad etadi.
why.ru: Text 1: ребёнок, потративший деньги зря, «has learned something»; Text 2: карманные деньги «teaches children how to handle money».

By agreeing that the garden is of little use for most months of the school year
By suggesting that students should grow their vegetables at home instead
By claiming that the school has no need for a court big enough for matches

made the carrots under it taste sweeter.
caused the soil under it to crack.

the teacher had given the two classes two different tests.
writing each word three times took much less practice time.
every student in every school learns best by working in pairs.

makes the bread bake faster in the oven.
changes the taste of the flour in the dough.
gives the bread of Sanjar its high rim.

ate from whichever bowl was nearer to the door.
did not much like the food in either bowl.
prefers fish to any other kind of food that it is ever given.

the kind of water in the shaded glass.

was most likely caused by the timetable on which they were watered.
shows that Gold plants cannot catch any kind of fungus at all.
proves that the soil in the greenhouse was much too poor for the Ruby plants.

the park keeper cleaning the water of the pond more often.

stem.en:
In the school chess club, a member may play in the town tournament only if she has won at least three club games this season. Nilufar has played six club games this season and lost four of them; none of her games ended in a draw. It follows that Nilufar ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?

options.en: cannot play in this season's town tournament.
has won enough games to enter the tournament.
will win her next game at the club.
has played fewer games than any other member.

why.en: Six games, four lost and no draws leave two wins, fewer than the three the rule asks "only if", so she cannot play in the tournament.
why.uz: Olti oʻyin, toʻrttasida magʻlubiyat, durang yoʻq: ikki gʻalaba, qoida «only if» talab qilgan uchtadan kam, demak u turnirda oʻynay olmaydi.
why.ru: Шесть партий, четыре поражения, ничьих нет: две победы, меньше трёх, которых требует «only if», значит, в турнир она не попадёт.

stem.en:
In the novel, the narrator's grandfather keeps a row of clay jars on the shelf above the stove. He labels each jar with a year, and every autumn he fills a new one with apricot jam. When the narrator comes home after many years away and reads the labels, she finds that the last three years have no jar. The narrator most likely realizes that her grandfather ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?

options.en: has not made his jam for the last three autumns.
has moved some of his jars to another shelf.
has never really liked apricot jam.
made more jam than ever in recent years.

why.en: A jar a year, labeled with its year, and none for the last three: the smallest step is that he has not made jam in those autumns.
why.uz: Har yili yil yozilgan bitta koʻza, oxirgi uch yilga esa koʻza yoʻq: eng kichik qadam — u oʻsha kuzlarda murabbo qilmagan.
why.ru: Каждый год банка с годом, а за последние три года банок нет: наименьший шаг — в те осени он варенья не варил.

stem.en:
The new sports hall will not open until the fire inspector has approved it, and the inspector will not visit until the builders have finished the second staircase. In October, the builders reported that the second staircase was still a month from being finished. It can be inferred that in October the hall ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?

options.en: could not yet have been approved by the fire inspector.
was already open to the students of the school.
had been approved but was not yet open.
would open as soon as the builders reported.

why.en: No visit until the staircase is done, no approval without a visit, no opening without approval; the staircase was unfinished, so no approval yet.

stem.en:
Davron found the front tire of his bicycle flat again this morning. A sharp stone stuck in the tire is a common cause, but he had run his fingers around the inside of the tire and found nothing. A worn valve can also leak, yet he had fitted a new valve last week. Then he noticed that the tire had been rubbing against the bent edge of the mudguard. The tire most likely went flat because ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?

options.en: the bent mudguard had worn through it.
a sharp stone was still caught inside it.
its new valve had started to leak air.
he had pumped it too hard the night before.

why.en: A stone and the valve are ruled out; the tire was rubbing on the bent mudguard, so that rubbing most likely wore a hole in it.

At the fruit stall by the school gate, the morning apples sell out only on days when the school is open. Last Saturday, Malohat came to the stall at ten and found that the apples had already sold out. Based on the text, it is most likely that last Saturday ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?

options.en: the school by the gate was open for the day.
the stall had fewer apples than usual.
the apples sell out every Saturday.
the school is never open on Saturdays.

why.en: The apples sell out "only on days when the school is open", and they sold out on Saturday, so the school was most likely open that day.
why.uz: Olmalar «only on days when the school is open» tugaydi va shanba kuni tugagan, demak oʻsha kuni maktab ochiq boʻlgan.
why.ru: Яблоки раскупают «only on days when the school is open», а в субботу их раскупили, значит, школа в тот день, вероятно, работала.

stem.en:
In the hills above the village, a spring that has run dry by July means that the shepherds must take their flocks up to the high pastures early, and a flock that goes up early always comes back down before the first snow. This year, the spring had run dry by the end of June. Based on the text, this year the flocks will most likely ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?

options.en: come back down before the first snow.
stay in the village for the whole summer.
come back down after the first snow.
find the high pastures dry as well.

why.en: Dry by the end of June is dry by July, so the flocks go up early, and early flocks come back before the first snow: two links to the key.

stem.en:
The museum lets visitors take photos in every room unless a sign at the door of the room says otherwise. In the textile room, a guard asked Timur to put his camera away, even though he had not noticed any sign. The guards always follow the rules of the museum. It is most likely that ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?

options.en: the textile room had a sign at its door that Timur missed.
taking photos is not allowed in any of the rooms of the museum.
the guard in the textile room was making up a rule of his own.
Timur had taken too many photos in the other rooms.

why.en: Photos are allowed "unless" a sign says otherwise, and the guards follow the rules, so the textile room most likely had a sign Timur did not see.
why.uz: Rasmga olish ruxsat, «unless» eshikda belgi boʻlsa; qoʻriqchi qoidaga amal qiladi, demak toʻqimachilik zalida Timur koʻrmagan belgi boʻlgan.
why.ru: Снимать можно, «unless» на двери есть табличка; охрана следует правилам, значит, у зала тканей была табличка, которую Тимур не заметил.

In the story, every evening for a year Hamid has left a bowl of milk on the step for the gray cat that lives under the woodshed. On the first warm evening of spring, the bowl is still full in the morning, and from under the woodshed come thin, high cries that Hamid has never heard before. The text most strongly suggests that the cat ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?

options.en: may have had kittens under the woodshed.
has left the neighborhood and the woodshed for good.
no longer likes the taste of milk.
is too ill to leave the woodshed.

why.en: The cat did not come for the milk, and new thin, high cries come from her shed: the smallest step the text supports is that she may have had kittens.

A member of the student council may be chosen as its chair only after two full years on the council, and the chair is chosen once a year, each September. Gulnora joined the council in September of her eighth-grade year and has stayed on it since. The earliest she could become chair is ______

in September of her ninth-grade year.

why.en: Joining in September of grade eight, she completes two full years in September of grade ten, the first choice of a chair she can enter.

stem.en:
Two samples of the same paint were left on a sunny wall for a summer, one on a white board and one on a black board. By autumn, the paint on the black board had faded much more. The paint maker first suspected the rain, but both boards hung under the same roof edge and got equally wet. Since the black board would have grown hotter in the sun, the extra fading ______

Which choice most logically completes the text?

options.en: may have been caused by the greater heat of the black board.
was caused by the rain that fell more heavily on the black board.
proves that all paint fades faster on dark surfaces.
shows that the white board was kept in the shade.

why.en: Same paint, same wall, equal rain: the rain is ruled out, and the black board ran hotter, so the heat may explain the extra fading.
